context:
1) Define and document canonical run_type vocabulary for query rows and
synthetic rows.
2) Add explicit producer-side stamping in SQL standard/throughput/maintenance
paths so run_type is present before normalization.
3) Propagate run_type into enhanced QueryExecution phase objects.
4) Keep fallback inference as compatibility-only safety net (not primary path).
5) Add contract tests that fail if any producer emits query rows without run_type.
description:
Query result rows currently rely on fallback inference for `run_type` in several
paths (especially SQL `standard` execution), while other paths set run_type
explicitly (`warmup`/`measurement`, and DataFrame metadata/summary rows).

This creates ambiguity and repeated fallback logic in normalization/schema code,
and can cause inconsistent downstream analytics semantics when producer paths
omit run_type.

This TODO defines canonical run_type semantics and ensures all producer paths
explicitly stamp run_type before result building/export. It also aligns
enhanced execution-phase objects and adds contract tests so missing run_type
cannot regress silently.

anti_patterns.instead: keep run_type as per-row execution role
anti_patterns.why: run mode is already carried by `test_execution_type`

anti_patterns.dont: remove fallback inference in query normalization immediately
anti_patterns.instead: retain compatibility while enforcing explicit tagging for new producer output

preserves.behavior: Backward compatibility for loading historical results without explicit run_type remains intact via normalization fallback
DataFrame metadata/summary synthetic rows keep their current run_type values (`metadata`/`summary`)
Existing power/throughput behavior where warmup rows are excluded from primary timing metrics remains unchanged
`test_execution_type` continues to represent run mode (`standard|power|throughput|maintenance|combined`) and is NOT replaced by run_type
